Subject: DPA questions: subprocessors list + breach notice timing

Grace —

Thanks for the quick DPA. Two quick items our legal team asked to confirm before we move to signature:

1) Subprocessors: we received an attached CSV of your current subprocessors; can you confirm whether any of these are transferring data outside the EU/US (we're US-based but have EU users)? We need explicit confirmation for our privacy team.

2) Incident notification cadence: our SOC requires initial notification within 24 hours for high-severity incidents and a follow-up plan within 72 hours. Your current redline mentions 72h notification — would Redwood accept a 24h initial notice for confirmed severe incidents, with 72h follow-up?

We prefer DocuSign for execution — please send an envelope to legal@acme-example.com when ready.

Best,
Sam

Hi Sam —

Thanks — appreciate the clarity. Short answers up front:
- Subprocessor transfers: most subprocessors are US-based cloud providers; a small set (inference acceleration partners) operate in EU regions and may process EU-origin data. We'll provide a short table confirming locations.
- Notification cadence: Redwood can do an initial notification within 24 hours for confirmed incidents that meet the severity threshold; our standard DPA language historically referenced 72h for initial notice — happy to accept a 24h initial notice for "confirmed severe" incidents and keep a 72h follow-up/update cadence.

I'm looping in Aditya (legal) to propose formal redline language to add to the DPA and Marissa to coordinate DocuSign routing once legal confirms.

Grace O'Connor

On Sat, 29 Aug 2026 at 09:12 AM, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai> wrote:

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: DPA questions: subprocessors list + breach notice timing

Sam —

Thanks for flagging. Proposed compromise redline (we can insert into the DPA as a short paragraph in Section 7 - "Security Incidents"):

"Notification and Cooperation. For confirmed security incidents materially affecting Customer Data, Redwood will provide: (i) initial written notice to Customer within twenty-four (24) hours of Redwood's confirmation that a security incident has occurred and is likely to materially affect Customer Data (the "Initial Notice"); (ii) a subsequent update within seventy-two (72) hours describing known scope, affected data classes, and immediate mitigation steps; and (iii) reasonable ongoing status updates until the incident is resolved. Redwood will cooperate with Customer in subsequent forensic reviews and regulatory notifications, providing reasonable assistance and documentation within thirty (30) days where feasible. If Redwood is unable to provide Initial Notice within twenty-four (24) hours due to ongoing investigation, Redwood will notify Customer of the delay and provide a best-effort timeline for the Initial Notice."

We also propose adding: "Redwood will notify Customer of the identities and function of any affected subprocessors within the Initial Notice where known; otherwise Redwood will include that information in the seventy-two (72) hour update."

This keeps the 24h ask for confirmed severe incidents, keeps the 72h follow-up, and adds subprocessor transparency.

Two operational notes:
- If Acme requires strict 24h notice for all incidents (including suspected ones), we need to quantify operational burden and may need to tie to severity/confirmed threshold.
- For cross-border transfers, we'll add the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) as an appendix and a statement that subprocessors will be bound by equivalent terms.

Please confirm and we'll prepare a redline to send to your legal.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Head of Legal (Privacy)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: DPA_redline_Grace_v2.docx

2) For the thirty (30) day forensic materials commitment, can you commit to providing prioritized evidence (logs, timelines) within fifteen (15) days when ACME is coordinating regulatory filings?

If you can accept 15 days for prioritized forensic evidence in regulatory circumstances, we can proceed to DocuSign. Please send the envelope to legal@acme-example.com and copy Sam and me.
